label: Detach rite to new faith
summary: Splits a rite off from its current faith into a brand-new faith, founded by the character.
details: The character it runs on becomes the founder of the new faith. The new faith can be saved as a named scope with `save_scope_as`, so later effects can use it. Vanilla uses it for heresy-style splits, with the rite given as a saved scope or a rite key.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The rite to detach from its faith.
fields.values: a rite, e.g. a saved scope or a rite key

fields.name: save_scope_as
fields.text: A name under which the newly created faith is saved for later use.

label: Forbid exposing secret
summary: Forbids a character from exposing this secret.
details: It runs on a secret. The character written as the value is the one who may no longer expose it.

label: Pause succession calculation
summary: Switches off the game's succession calculations.
details: Requests for new calculations are still queued, so they can be run later (see the enable-and-run effect). Vanilla only ever writes `yes`.

label: Disband confederation
summary: Disbands the confederation and destroys its title.
details: It runs on a confederation. Vanilla only writes `yes`.

label: Divide war chest
summary: Gives out the war chest of a great holy war, in full or in part.
details: By default the attackers receive it. Gold, piety and prestige are all handed out unless you switch one off with `no`. Vanilla calls it with an empty block, or with `gold = no`, `prestige = no`, `defenders = yes` and a `fraction`. The game's documentation names the share field `faction`, but vanilla writes `fraction`.

fields.name: defenders
fields.text: Give the war chest to the defenders instead of the attackers.

fields.name: fraction
fields.text: The part of the war chest to give out, where 1 is all of it (vanilla uses 0.2).

label: Divorce
summary: Divorces the character from the given person.
details: The character it runs on and the target character are the two spouses. Vanilla gives the target as a saved scope, `root`, `prev` or a link like `primary_spouse`.

label: Hand out titles after holy war
summary: Hands out titles in the taken kingdom to the attacker's beneficiaries of a great holy war.
details: People are made vassals according to the de jure liege inside the conquered kingdom. County garrisons and levies are refilled. The value is a saved title-and-vassal-change object; vanilla always passes `scope:change`.

label: Downgrade building
summary: Replaces a building in the holding with the previous building of its line, if there is one.
details: Name any building of the line and it is downgraded one level. It runs on a province. The game's documentation says there must already be another building of the same type in place, otherwise the effect fails with an error. Duchy capital buildings also fail if the province does not support them. Vanilla does not use it, so this rests on the game's documentation only.

label: Skill duel
summary: Picks one outcome at random, weighted by comparing a skill of the character against a value or another character.
details: The body works like `random_list`: each entry has a weight and effects. The skill difference (or the scripted value) is available inside the entries as `scope:duel_value`, and the opponent as `scope:duel_target`. With several skills, their average is used. The game's documentation says the difference is normally between -20 and 20, so weights should be in a similar range. A weight can fall to 0 through modifiers, and then that outcome cannot happen. Vanilla mostly writes `skill`, `value` (often a named script value) and `target`.

fields.name: skill
fields.values: a skill such as diplomacy, intrigue, learning, prowess, stewardship

fields.name: skills
fields.text: Several skills at once; their average is compared.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The character to compare against. Needs a skill.

fields.name: value
fields.text: A number or script value to compare against, or the whole duel value if no skill is given.

fields.name: challenge_variable
fields.text: A saved variable to use in the comparison; it needs a localized name.

fields.name: localization
fields.text: An entry of the effect localization database used to describe the duel.

label: Else
summary: Runs its effects when the `if` (or `else_if`) just before it did not run.
details: It must follow an `if` or `else_if` block. It has no limit of its own. Vanilla uses it very often.

label: Else if
summary: Runs its effects when the earlier `if` or `else_if` did not run and its own limit is met.
details: It must follow an `if` or `else_if` block, and has its own `limit` with triggers. Vanilla nearly always gives it a limit.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: The conditions that must be true for this branch to run.

label: Resume succession calculation
summary: Switches succession calculations back on and runs all that are waiting in the queue.
details: It is the counterpart of the effect that disables them. Vanilla only writes `yes`.

label: Enact budgets
summary: Calculates the character's budget rates from the allocation modifiers and current income.
details: This version applies the costs and the opinion effects.

label: Enact budgets (initial)
summary: Calculates the character's budget rates from the allocation modifiers and current income, without costs or opinion effects.
details: It also recalculates the modifiers.

label: Enact budgets, no costs
summary: Calculates the character's budget rates from the allocation modifiers and current income, without costs or opinion effects.
details: Compare the plain version, which charges costs and applies opinion effects.

label: Enact budgets, no costs or opinions
summary: Calculates the character's budget rates from the allocation modifiers and current income, without costs or opinion effects.
details: The game's documentation describes it the same way as the no-costs version. Vanilla does not use this one.

label: Enact budgets, no opinions
summary: Calculates the character's budget rates from the allocation modifiers and current income, charging costs but applying no opinion effects.
details: Vanilla does not use it.

label: End diarchy
summary: Ends the diarchy of the character.
details: The game's documentation shows `yes/no`; vanilla only writes `yes`.

label: End inspiration sponsorship
summary: Stops the sponsorship of the given inspiration.
details: Vanilla gives the inspiration as a saved scope (mostly `scope:inspiration`) or `prev`.

label: End pregnancy
summary: Ends the character's pregnancy without a birth.
details: The game's documentation says only 'end a pregnancy'. It does not say whether this counts as a miscarriage or an abortion.

label: End scheme
summary: Ends the scheme and removes it, with no other effect.
details: The game's documentation says it has no other effect. Vanilla uses it very often.

label: End situation
summary: Ends the situation.
details: Vanilla uses it once, with `yes`.

label: End story
summary: Ends the story and runs its on_end effects.
details: After this the story can no longer be reached.

label: End struggle
summary: Ends the struggle.
details: Vanilla mostly writes `yes`. A few uses write a name instead, such as an ending decision or a template placeholder; the game's documentation does not say what a name does there.

label: End tributary contract
summary: Ends the character's current tributary contract.
details: Vanilla only writes `yes`.

label: End war
summary: Ends the war with the chosen result.
details: Write `attacker` or `defender` to let that side win, or `white_peace` for a white peace. Vanilla also uses `invalidated`, which the game's documentation does not mention.

label: Enshrine artifact
summary: Lets the character place an artifact in a holy site.
details: It fires the on_actions for an artifact being enshrined and, if one is replaced, for one being removed. To avoid that, use the normal inventory ownership effects instead.

fields.name: holy_site
fields.text: The holy site that receives the artifact.

fields.name: slot
fields.text: Which slot of the site to use.

label: Equip artifact
summary: Makes the artifact's owner equip it.
details: It fails if the slot of that artifact already holds equipment.

label: Equip artifact, replacing
summary: Makes the artifact's owner equip it, replacing another artifact if needed.
details: If all slots of its type are full, the first held artifact is replaced.

label: Log error
summary: Writes a message to the error log when it runs.
details: The message can be a localization string; ROOT, SCOPE and PREV can be used in it. Vanilla's messages report situations that should not happen, such as a missing scope.

label: Log scopes
summary: Writes the current scope to the error log when it runs.
details: With `yes` the full scope information is logged, with `no` only the current scope. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Log error with stack trace
summary: Writes a message to the error log, followed by a stack trace.
details: The message can be a localization string; ROOT, SCOPE and PREV can be used in it. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Execute decision
summary: Executes the given decision for the character.
details: The value is the decision's key. Vanilla uses it with decisions such as commission artifact and tribute missions.

label: Expand clerical region
summary: Adds the de jure counties of another title to the clerical region title.
details: It runs on the clerical region title; the value is the title whose counties are added. Only adjacent counties that are not already in another clerical region are added, so it can find nothing to add.

label: Expose scheme
summary: Exposes the scheme to the defender.
details: Vanilla only writes `yes`.

label: Expose scheme agent
summary: Exposes the given character as an agent of this scheme.
details: It runs on a scheme.

label: Expose scheme to character
summary: Exposes the scheme to the given character.
details: It runs on a scheme. Vanilla uses it once.

label: Expose secret
summary: Exposes the secret, with the given character as the one who exposes it.
details: Vanilla mostly passes `root`, a saved scope or `prev`.

label: Detach war from faction
summary: Removes the war that is currently tied to the faction.
details: Vanilla only writes `yes`.

label: Start faction war
summary: Makes the faction start its war against its target.
details: Vanilla mostly uses an empty block; a few uses give a `title` for the war.

fields.name: title
fields.text: An optional title for the war; the game's documentation says nothing more.
fields.values: a title, e.g. a saved scope or a title key
